laws.rule: Hegra (AlUla) can be visited only on an organised tour (coach or private premium 4x4), from SAR 95; self-driving is not allowed. Tours are limited each day, so pre-booking is highly recommended. (No RBA rate for SAR; at the Saudi Central Bank (SAMA) rate of 30 October 2026 crossed via the RBA USD rate of 30 October 2026, A$1 = about 2.64 SAR: SAR 95 ≈ A$35.98)
laws.heading: FAQ

laws.rule: Stay on the designated walking paths; entering non-designated areas, including the tombs, and touching the engravings is prohibited.

Australia's Smartraveller advice says only Muslims are allowed to enter Makkah (Mecca) and Madinah (Medina). The Visit Saudi help centre is reported to word it more narrowly (non-Muslims with a visa may visit the city of Madinah but not the Prophet's Mosque and its premises), but that page could not be opened, so the two readings are shown side by side. Ask the Saudi Ministry of Tourism or an embassy which applies before planning a stop.
laws.heading: Entry and exit

laws.rule: AlUla heritage-site visitor code requires designated walking paths and roads, no entering non-designated areas such as tombs, no climbing or removing natural/heritage material, and no fires. It sets a 30 km/h driving limit and designated parking. These are heritage-operator visitor terms, not the speed limit or camping law throughout Medina Province.

Hegra Premium Tour conditions describe a guided, two-hour vehicle tour meeting at Hegra Visitor Centre, with a private vehicle seating up to seven and a guide potentially shared between two cars, maximum fourteen. Maintenance/excavation can close some areas. This is this ticket product's access format, not evidence that every Hegra ticket has the same vehicle/group size.

culture-and-protocol.cultural_authority: Royal Commission for AlUla / Experience AlUla, for its heritage visitor sites and this tour product only.
culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: Stay on designated heritage paths, do not enter non-designated tombs, climb monuments, mark rock surfaces, touch/pour water on engravings or remove heritage material. The Premium Tour recommends outdoor clothes and closed-toe walking shoes/boots; the recommendation is not turned into a province-wide clothing law.
culture-and-protocol.photography_and_story_permissions: Heritage rules say take nothing but pictures, but the website has separate restrictive event-photography clauses. Personal heritage photographs and event/attendee recording are not treated as the same permission; obtain product/event-specific consent before recording people or performances. Community storytelling permissions not yet checked.
culture-and-protocol.note: Site-specific conservation and operator protocol, not all Medina communities or a claim about national religious dress law.
